title: Portable recording units and the RCA Victor clockwork disc recorder
summary: Visiting companies recorded on portable equipment in hotels and dance halls since the 1920s; he describes RCA Victor's weight-driven portable disc recorder.

RCA Victor had a portable disc recording unit gigantic thing you know disc recorders in those days weighed a couple of thousand pounds and this one was run by a clockwork mechanism literally there was a huge weight that they cranked up and then by gravity through a clockwork type mechanism drove the the cutting lathe and the reason for it was it was it was absolutely free of any power source anomalies for instance the power being off in voltage or frequency or sudden interruptions you know those kinds of things this device was it was a marvelous device in the sense it was probably one of the last things that the mechanical age turned out if you if you if you've ever seen mostly in museums now old iron working machines and those kinds of things they were gorgeous pieces of work themselves you know some of them quite intricate you know to make some machine pieces that that whole that whole craft has almost disappeared there are few people yet who are extraordinary in that sense but they're you know probably working for NASA
